principle.author: G. K. Chesterton
principle.sentence: He did not understand that their one essential historical principle, the one law truly graven on their hearts, was the great and comforting statement that Queen Anne is dead.

principle.author: Walt Whitman
principle.sentence: Thou seething principle! thou well-kept, latent germ! thou centre!

principled.author: George Eliot
principled.sentence: I am sure he is a very deserving, well-principled young man,” said Rosamond, with a neat air of patronage in return for Mrs.

unprincipled.author: Thomas Hardy
unprincipled.sentence: A warmth overspread his face: surely she was not so unprincipled as to flirt in a fair!

unprincipled.author: George Eliot
unprincipled.sentence: Casaubon’s curate to be; doubtless an excellent man who would go to heaven (for Celia wished not to be unprincipled), but the corners of his mouth were so unpleasant.

unprincipled.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
unprincipled.sentence: Was it that houses and lands, offices, wine, horses, dress, luxury, are had by unprincipled men, whilst the saints are poor and despised; and that a compensation is to be made to these last hereafter, by giving them the like gratifications another day,--bank stock and doubloons,[96] venison and champagne?

unprincipled.author: Henry David Thoreau
unprincipled.sentence: His vote is of no more worth than that of any unprincipled foreigner or hireling native, who may have been bought.

unprincipled.author: Herman Melville
unprincipled.sentence: High times, indeed, if unprincipled young rakes like him are to be permitted to invade the sanctity of domestic bliss; though do what the Bashaw will, he cannot keep the most notorious Lothario out of his bed; for, alas! all fish bed in common.

unprincipled.author: Jane Austen
unprincipled.sentence: Her indignation would have been still stronger than it was, had she not witnessed that embarrassment which seemed to speak a consciousness of his own misconduct, and prevented her from believing him so unprincipled as to have been sporting with the affections of her sister from the first, without any design that would bear investigation.
